title: 1st Abyss 1st Matter In Negation There Is No Mutual Support

questions.question: In the passage, what happens to statements that prove something to be true?
questions.answer: They come together around one reality, so they support each other.

questions.question: Why do statements of denial not strengthen one another in the same way?
questions.answer: Because each denial comes from a person’s own limited view, so they stay separate instead of joining into one proof.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the large number of unbelievers and deniers?
questions.answer: Their being many does not make their position stronger against belief.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should be protected from doubt?
questions.answer: A believer’s firm faith and certainty should be protected.

questions.question: Whose denials are said to have caused confusion for some people in this age?
questions.answer: The denials of European philosophers are said to have caused doubt.

questions.question: How are the people affected by those denials described in the passage?
questions.answer: They are described as unfortunate people who were deceived.

questions.question: What harmful result came to their faith?
questions.answer: Their certainty was ruined.

questions.question: What greater loss followed the destruction of certainty?
questions.answer: Their eternal happiness was wiped out.

questions.question: What everyday reality is mentioned to show how serious this issue is?
questions.answer: Many people die every day and reach their appointed time.

questions.question: How do deniers wrongly present death?
questions.answer: They present it as total and everlasting destruction.

questions.question: What image is used to show how near death and the grave are to people?
questions.answer: The grave is shown as always open and always facing people.

questions.question: According to the passage, how does denial affect a person’s life emotionally?
questions.answer: It fills life with deep bitterness and sorrow.

questions.question: What does the passage say faith really is for a human being?
questions.answer: It is a huge blessing and the core of true life.

questions.question: What main contrast is being made throughout the passage?
questions.answer: The passage contrasts the weakness of denial with the strength and life-giving value of faith.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the first two sentences of the passage?
questions.answer: Proofs of truth unite, but denials split apart.

questions.question: What causes denial to become “multiple” in the passage?
questions.answer: Each person speaks from his own opinion or belief instead of from one shared certainty.

questions.question: If many people reject belief, what should a Muslim understand from this passage?
questions.answer: A large crowd rejecting something does not make falsehood true.

questions.question: What attitude does the passage teach toward a believer’s certainty?
questions.answer: It should not be shaken or disturbed by doubts.

questions.question: What source of doubt is especially criticized in the passage?
questions.answer: Philosophical denials coming from Europe are especially criticized.

questions.question: What happened to some people after listening to those denials?
questions.answer: They fell into doubt and lost strong faith.

questions.question: Why is losing certainty presented as more than just an intellectual problem?
questions.answer: Because it harms a person’s hereafter, not just his thoughts.

questions.question: What two human experiences are mentioned to make the discussion personal and urgent?
questions.answer: Death and the approach of a person’s fixed lifetime are mentioned.

questions.question: How does faith change the way death is understood?
questions.answer: Faith keeps death from being seen as meaningless destruction.

questions.question: How does denial change the way death is understood?
questions.answer: Denial makes death look like endless nonexistence.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest the grave becomes for a denier?
questions.answer: It becomes a frightening sign of destruction.

questions.question: Why does that view of the grave poison life?
questions.answer: Because it fills a person with constant fear and sadness.

questions.question: Based on the passage, why is faith called a blessing?
questions.answer: It gives meaning, hope, and real life instead of despair.

questions.question: In the passage, which is shown as having a shared result: affirmation or negation?
questions.answer: Affirmation is shown as having one shared result.

questions.question: What is the effect of that shared result?
questions.answer: Each true confirming statement adds strength to the others.

questions.question: Why can separate denials not build one strong case together?
questions.answer: Because they are based on different personal viewpoints and do not point to one united reality.

questions.question: What false impression might people get from seeing many unbelievers?
questions.answer: They might think unbelief is stronger just because more people hold it.

questions.question: How does the passage correct that impression?
questions.answer: It says numbers and outward dominance do not give real weight to denial.

questions.question: What responsibility is mentioned regarding believers?
questions.answer: People should avoid causing doubts in the hearts of believers.

questions.question: What group is mentioned as spreading doubt in this age?
questions.answer: European philosophers are mentioned.

questions.question: What word best describes the people who followed those doubts: guided, careful, or deceived?
questions.answer: Deceived.

questions.question: What two losses do those deceived people suffer?
questions.answer: They lose certainty in faith and lose eternal happiness.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the daily number of deaths?
questions.answer: To show that death is constant and close, so beliefs about it matter greatly.

questions.question: What does the passage say deniers remove from death?
questions.answer: They remove its meaning as a departure from this world.

questions.question: Into what do they turn death instead?
questions.answer: They turn it into the idea of endless extinction.

questions.question: What ongoing threat does the grave hold for the denier in the passage?
questions.answer: It keeps confronting him with the fear of annihilation.

questions.question: What emotional result follows from that fear?
questions.answer: Life becomes bitter and full of grief.

questions.question: What final truth does the reader is asked to recognize?
questions.answer: Faith is an enormous gift and the heart of real living.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the relationship between one proof and another proof for the same truth?
questions.answer: They back each other up because they point to the same conclusion.

questions.question: How does it describe the relationship between one denial and another denial?
questions.answer: They remain scattered because each one depends on a different personal claim.

questions.question: Why is denial linked to personal viewpoint in the passage?
questions.answer: Because a denier speaks from what he thinks or sees, not from a united and complete truth.

questions.question: What should not impress a believer according to the passage: the truth of faith or the crowd of deniers?
questions.answer: The crowd of deniers should not impress a believer.

questions.question: In this passage, what is more important than numbers?
questions.answer: Real truth and certainty are more important than numbers.

questions.question: What harm is described when doubt enters a believer’s heart?
questions.answer: Strong faith becomes weak or destroyed.

questions.question: Who are said to have introduced such doubts in this age?
questions.answer: European philosophers are said to have done that.

questions.question: What happened to the people who were taken in by those ideas?
questions.answer: They lost confidence in faith and were spiritually harmed.

questions.question: What does the passage say was erased along with their certainty?
questions.answer: Their everlasting happiness was erased.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect this issue to death?
questions.answer: Because everyone faces death, so how a person understands it shapes his whole life.

questions.question: What healthy meaning of death is denied by unbelief in the passage?
questions.answer: Its meaning as leaving this world, not ending forever.

questions.question: What dark meaning is given to death by denial?
questions.answer: It is treated as complete and endless nothingness.

questions.question: How is the grave pictured for someone without faith?
questions.answer: It is pictured as a constant warning of destruction.

questions.question: What does that picture do to a person’s everyday life?
questions.answer: It makes life painful and filled with sorrow.

questions.question: What two things is faith called at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: A great blessing and the essence of life.

questions.question: What single feature makes affirmations strong in the passage?
questions.answer: They all point to one truth, so they can join together.

questions.question: What feature makes negations weak in the passage?
questions.answer: They are divided among many personal opinions and do not unite.

questions.question: What mistaken idea about unbelief does the passage warn against?
questions.answer: It warns against thinking unbelief is powerful just because many people appear to follow it.

questions.question: What must people avoid doing to believers?
questions.answer: They must avoid making them doubtful about their faith.

questions.question: What outside influence is named as a cause of doubt in this age?
questions.answer: The denying ideas of European philosophers.

questions.question: How are some of the people influenced by those ideas characterized?
questions.answer: They are described as people who were fooled and harmed.

questions.question: What happened first to these people’s faith?
questions.answer: Their certainty was shaken and destroyed.

questions.question: What happened next in terms of the hereafter?
questions.answer: Their eternal joy was lost.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that many people die each day?
questions.answer: To remind readers that death is not far away or rare.

questions.question: How is death interpreted by people of denial according to the passage?
questions.answer: They see it as permanent disappearance.

questions.question: What is the grave like for such people?
questions.answer: It is like an ever-present doorway they fear leads to destruction.

questions.question: What does this belief do to their emotional state?
questions.answer: It makes their life taste bitter with sadness.

questions.question: What should a thoughtful Muslim appreciate after reading this?
questions.answer: He should value faith deeply because it gives hope, meaning, and true life.

questions.question: What is the difference between affirmation and negation in the way they combine?
questions.answer: Affirmation gathers into one strong support, while negation stays divided into many separate claims.

questions.question: Why does the passage say each denial stands on its own?
questions.answer: Because each one is tied to what a particular person thinks or believes.

questions.question: What conclusion should be drawn from that about the many deniers of faith?
questions.answer: Their large number does not give their denial real strength.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should believers be careful not to lose?
questions.answer: They should be careful not to lose certainty in faith.

questions.question: What kind of people are said to have spread harmful doubt in this age?
questions.answer: Philosophers from Europe who denied belief.

questions.question: What result did their ideas have on some people?
questions.answer: Some people fell into hesitation and lost their firm faith.

questions.question: Why is this loss described as a disaster, not a small mistake?
questions.answer: Because it destroys a person’s eternal success, not just one opinion.

questions.question: What two realities of human life are used to show the seriousness of belief and denial?
questions.answer: Daily death and the fixed end of each person’s life.

questions.question: What true meaning of death is taken away by denial?
questions.answer: Its meaning as a transfer from this world.

questions.question: What false meaning is put in its place?
questions.answer: The idea that death is endless extinction.

questions.question: How does the grave appear to a person who accepts that false meaning?
questions.answer: It looks like a constant threat of being wiped out.

questions.question: What is the effect of this on the person’s experience of life?
questions.answer: His life becomes bitter and weighed down by grief.

questions.question: What is the final message of the passage about faith?
questions.answer: Faith is a tremendous blessing that gives life its deepest meaning.

questions.question: Which is presented as life-giving in the passage: faith or denial?
questions.answer: Faith is presented as life-giving.
